Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Monday of every month at 6:00 p.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the Community Services Department via email at
kshigenaga@cityofsanmarino.org or by phone at (626) 300­0791 prior to the meeting for
assistance.

  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 (AB 361)

each teleconference location from which a member will be participating in a public meeting.

MINUTES
  REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE SAN MARINO RECREATION COMMISSION
  MONDAY, NOVEMBER 14, 2022 AT 6:00 P.M.
  BARTH ROOM, CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY

CALL TO ORDER: Chairperson Yen called the regular meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the Barth
Room, located at 1890 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California 91108.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Chairperson Yen led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL:  PRESENT: Commissioner Tam, Commissioner Tsai, Commissioner Wu,
  Vice Chairperson Solan, and Chairperson Yen

  ABSENT: None

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

COMMISSIONER REPORTS

Commissioners shared the following programming feedback, requests, and ideas they received from
neighbors and friends:
  • Chairperson Yen: more cultural, educational, and sports youth activities afterschool; more
  indoor and outdoor sporting activities; more youth offerings on school sites; want a
  community pool; enjoyed Trunk or Treat; more events with music and movies; want a 5K
  run around Lacy Park
  • Vice Chairperson Solan: more music and art classes for youth; want a community pool and
  more meeting space; love the preschool program
  • Commissioner Tam: more indoor activities related to language and arts; want a community
  pool; want a year-round tots program
  • Commissioner Tsai: love the Senior Wellness Calls; more movie nights at Lacy Park
  throughout the year; want a Mother’s Day picnic; more adult lectures and programming
  focusing on exercise; love the home decorating contests; shared about inconsistencies in
  start times for contract classes

There was discussion by the Commission about the programming that still occurs at Stoneman
Building; how program ideas can or will be considered by the Recreation Commission for the
upcoming budget cycle; if the prior Strategic Plan will continue to guide operations until a new plan
is put in place; if additional contract classes will be considered if additional programming space
becomes available; and potential repartitioning of City properties, like Lacy Park.

Director Johnson presented the staff report.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

3. TRUNK OR TREAT & MOVIE NIGHT EVENT DEBRIEF

Director Johnson presented the staff report.

There was discussion by the Commission about how successful the event was at creating a sense of
involvement; staff appearing overwhelmed; the impact of increased community events as per the
Recreation Re-Envisioning Plan on existing staff; the non-resident attendance at the event; how
performance data can be used to support funding requests from the State or County; and if staff
have sought out volunteers to help support medium to large events.
